entries.proposition: NOT a dose-response: clemastine at one stated dose, given P21 to P58, i.e. after the knockout at P10-12 and after weaning, not in the infant window.
entries.snippet: clemastine fumarate (10 mg/kg), a first-generation antihistamine with established remyelination-promoting effects, was administered once daily from P21 to P58

entries.proposition: Pdk1 icKO mice remained viable and did not exhibit spontaneous seizures or early lethality, unlike the constitutive Pdk1 cKO (Olig1-Cre) model; clemastine was tested only in the icKO (entry 2 and Methods). Induction at P10-12 is in Methods (entry 11).
entries.snippet: In contrast to the constitutive Pdk1 cKO mouse model (Pdk1fl/fl;Olig1-Cre) [22], Pdk1 icKO mice remained viable and did not exhibit spontaneous seizures or early lethality.
entries.anchor: Results / Postnatal PDK1 deletion impairs OPC differentiation

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Quote carries viability and no seizures in the icKO; the induction age and the constitutive model details are in other entries. Proposition narrowed to the quote and cross-referenced.

entries.proposition: MBP immunostaining was markedly enhanced in clemastine-treated Pdk1 icKO mice relative to saline-treated mutants (Fig 4F-G). entries.proposition: Fig 4 legend: Olig2 n = 3 per group (p < 0.01) and ASPA n = 3-4 per group (p < 0.01) in saline- versus clemastine-treated mutants. The MBP n and the TrueGold star-versus-p mismatch are in other legend panels, not quoted here.
entries.snippet: (C) Quantification of Olig2+ cells. Clemastine treatment significantly increased the number of Olig2+ cells in Pdk1 icKO mice compared to saline-treated mutants. entries.proposition: Hyperexcitability was not measured (no EEG or excitability assay in the text or supplement). Neuronal activity is read as c-Fos+ cell counts (n = 6 per genotype) and, in the untreated knockout against controls, mEPSC amplitude and frequency (n = 3 animals per genotype); both are reduced in the knockout.
entries.snippet: Quantification of c-Fos+ cells showed a significant decrease in the hippocampus of Pdk1 icKO mice compared to controls. Data are presented as mean ± SEM (n = 6 per genotype; ∗, p < 0.05). (G) Represented mEPSC traces in control (black) and Pdk1 icKO (red) mice. Scale bar: 20 mV, 2 s. (H) Averaged mEPSC traces from control (black) and Pdk1 icKO (red) neurons. Aligned mEPSC peaks and the average trace are shown in dark color from a typical neuron. Scale bar: 20 mV, 20 ms. (I) Cumulative probability plot and quantification of mEPSC amplitudes. Pdk1 icKO mice exhibited a significant reduction in mEPSC amplitude compared to controls. Data are presented as mean ± SEM (n = 3 per genotype; ∗∗, p < 0.01). (J) Cumulative probability plot and quantification of mEPSC inter-event intervals. mEPSC frequency was significantly decreased in Pdk1 icKO mice. Data are presented as mean ± SEM (n = 3 per genotype; ∗, p < 0.05).

entries.proposition: In the icKO, clemastine significantly raised c-Fos+ cell counts versus saline (n = 6 per group, p < 0.01 in the legend); the authors read this as restored hippocampal neuronal activation. c-Fos is an immediate-early-gene positive cell count, not an excitability or EEG measure.
entries.snippet: We next assessed whether synaptic restoration translated into improved neuronal activity in vivo. Immunostaining for c-Fos revealed that clemastine treatment significantly increased the number of c-Fos+ cells in Pdk1 icKO mice, indicating restored hippocampal neuronal activation (Fig. 5E and F).
entries.anchor: Results / Deletion of PDK1 impairs synaptogenesis

entries.proposition: No body weight, exposure, histamine-related or sedation-labelled measure was found for clemastine in the text, legends or supplement; the Discussion relies on an established-safety statement. entries.proposition: Mechanism: clemastine restores Akt T308 and S6 phosphorylation; the muscarinic M1 antagonism route is named as an unexplored alternative.
entries.snippet: Clemastine treatment was associated with restoration of Akt and mTORC1 signaling in Pdk1 icKO mice, providing a plausible mechanistic basis for its observed therapeutic effects. Interestingly, clemastine has been reported to exert pro-myelination effects through antagonism of muscarinic receptor 1 (M1R) [59,60], raising the possibility of crosstalk between M1R signaling and Akt-mTOR pathway regulation in oligodendroglial cells, which warrants further investigation.
